summary: Candidate B closely implements the frozen contract; candidate A substantially expands and changes the API and retry machinery in direct conflict with it.
reasons: B adds the exact required Upload signature with opts ...FilesOption, uses multipartbody.NewFile("file", fileName, content), and delegates to FilesService.Add.
B preserves Add and existing FilesOption behavior, while A introduces UploadFileOption/FilesRequestOption, changes option return types, and bypasses Add by duplicating its request and response logic.
A adds explicitly forbidden association fields and modifies global raw-body retry semantics, reader ownership, multipart helpers, documentation, and unrelated behavior.
B validates filename/content before encoding and naturally propagates multipartbody.NewFile source-reader errors.
risks_a: Upload has the wrong public signature and existing FilesOption values are no longer uniformly accepted.
Direct Raw.Do usage duplicates Add behavior and risks future semantic drift.
Global seeker-based replay mutates unrelated retry and body-closing semantics; sharing one seeker across attempts is also fragile under concurrent request-body access or redirects.
risks_b: It adds an unrelated PersonsService.UploadPicture API, violating scope discipline and the requirement to add exactly the requested convenience API.
Upload tests do not verify uploaded content, validation failures, source-reader failures, or that the multipart payload itself is intact on every retry.
